items.stem: When only the background of an existing image needs to change, what is the preferred approach?

options.text: Use an edit so the rest of the image is preserved
options.rationale: Correct: an edit changes only the targeted region.

options.text: Regenerate the whole image from scratch each time
options.rationale: Regenerating risks changing the parts you wanted to keep.

options.text: Increase the resolution and nothing else
options.rationale: Resolution does not change the background.
A prompt is still needed to direct the edit.

items.explanation: Correct: an edit changes only the targeted region.

items.stem: Why should an image production workflow include a review and selection step?

options.text: Generations vary, so a review gate ensures only acceptable images ship
options.rationale: Correct: a review gate filters variable output against criteria.
A review step does not remove natural variation.
Rights considerations remain regardless of review.

items.explanation: Correct: a review gate filters variable output against criteria.

items.stem: Which TWO factors must be planned before running a large image-production batch? (Select TWO)

options.text: Content rights and safety of the images
options.rationale: Correct: rights and safety govern whether images can be used.

options.text: Cost and throughput of the batch
options.rationale: Correct: large batches have real cost and throughput limits.

options.text: A guarantee that output is identical to the prompt every time
options.rationale: Output varies and cannot be guaranteed identical.

options.text: Removing any shared accept or reject criteria
options.rationale: Shared criteria are needed, not removed.

items.explanation: Correct: rights and safety govern whether images can be used.
